rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WASTE DISPOSAL SYSTEM
rows.abstract: States the following --- "SECTION 3. Financial Assistance. The national government shall provide financial assistance to financially distressed cities or municipalities to cover the cost of designing and installing an efficient and effective systemof garbage collection and disposal.  The extent of financial assistance shall be up to a maximum of three percent (3%) of the Internation Revenue Allotment (IRA) of cities or municipalities in the preceding fiscal year and shall be according to the financial status of cities or municipalities as follows: (1)  6th class city or municipality - 100% of maximum; (2) 5th class city or municipality - 80% of maximum; (3) 4th class city of municipality - 60%; (4) 3rd class city or municipality - 40% ofmaximum; (5) 2nd class city or municipality - 20% of maximum; (6) 1st class city or municipality - 0%.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-05-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE AMOUNT OF TWO HUNDRED PESOS (P200.00) AS THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF APPLICATION FEE THAT CAN BE CHARGED BY AN EMPLOYER TO A JOB APPLICANT FOR LOCAL EMPLOYMENT
rows.abstract: Rationale:  A common problem encountered by job applicants is the excessive fees charged by companies. These fees are charged usually to cover expenses for medical examination, application form, aptitude and other tests, pictures and other requirements. These fees range from P300 to P1,000.00. Penalizes employees who fail to comply with or circumvent the provisions of this proposed measure with UNFAIR LABOR PRACTICE and a fine of P10,000.00.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1997-05-06

rows.abstract: Rationale: Kidnapping and drug trafficking still persist and remain rampant despite the instensified campaign launched by the Philippine National Police (PNP). It is therefore, essential, that in order to effect the capture, prosecution and finally,conviction of the leaders of these crime syndicates, special mechanisms must be put in place.> This bill proposes to create a Special Reward fund to bolster the cooperation and coordination between the citizenry and government law enforcement agencies in the capture, prosecution and conviction of the top most wanted drug lords and kidnap-for-rans on lords. rows.abstract: Rationale: Trafficking in women takes many forms and continues to thrive in a more sophisticated, technological and globalized dimensions. > Trafficking in women is closely associated  to the sex trade and should be given attention. Since the Philippines is a signatory to the 1949 Convention for the Suppression of the Traffic in Persons and of the Exploitation of the Prostitution of Others as well, it is committed to implement such Covenant and other relevant international instruments. "The Anti-Traffickin g in Filipino Women Act of 1996" Provides for the following --- (1) comprehensive measures in the suppression of trafficiking in women; (2) higher standards of rehabilitation and protection of victims of prostitution, sexual   ? , etc; ((3) definition of the various acts of trafficking; penalties for violators of this proposed measure; and (4) creation of an INTER-AGENCY COUNCIL against trafficking.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR A PROGRAM OF MODERNIZATION FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The current bill is intended to be a companion measure to the revised University Charter. It draws from the vision of U.P. Plan 2008, the University's strategic plan up to its first centennial and into the twenty-first century.  The U.P.Modernization Program seeks to provide Congressional support and resoruces to major areas which the University must develop to keep its lead in and provide support for the Philippine educational system, assure its place in the international system ofunviersitys, and enhance its capacity to respond to the major problems of our national life. "U.P. Modernization Program Act" Recommends the Program with these components: (1) Development of More Comprehensive Autonomous Campuses; (2) Expansion of CCenters of Excellence; (3) Creation of Cultural Complexes; (4) Expansion and Development of Training and Resource Centers; (5) Modernization of the PGH; and (6) Administrative System and Governance.

Declares the following --- "SEC. 1. The importation of garbage and waste materials for recycling including but not limited to the following: waste paper, acetate, iron or steel, carbon plated or coated with tin, paper board, corrugated paper, glass, silicon sands, plastics, metal scraps, and other solid waste materials is hereby prohibited." rows.abstract: Rationale: Seeks to update and revise our existing Arbitration Law pursuant to Republic Act 876 and adopt with modifications the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Model Law on Commercial Arbitration. The Model Law was adopted by the UNICITRAL in its eighteenth 18th session on June 21, 1985 after due deliberation and extensive consultation with arbitral institutions and individual experts on international comemrcial arbitration and was recommended to all States foradoption. rows.abstract: Rationale: The General Appropriations Act of 1997, however, allocates only P500 million for general registration of voters scheduled immediately after the barangay elections in May 1997 which is P1.5 billion short of the P2 billion funding requirement under R.A. No. 8189. The much-needed P2 billion will cover not only personal services and maintenance and other operating expenses but also the cost of voters ID cards for an estimated 40 million voters. > If this budgetary requirements is not met, the full intent of the law which is to cleanse the elctoral system of tampered and spurious lsits of voters shall be frustrated. The new list to be generated after the scheduled general registration will ensure the integity of the electoral resultss of the May 1998 national elections and all elections, plebiscites, referenda, initiatives and recalls thereafter.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The Free Public Secondary Education Act of 1988 has opened wider opportunities for young people in their quest for higher education. It develops when the amount of calories consumed as food and drink, exceeds the energy used for exercise and other metabolic processes. rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSPERSON FOR CHILDREN, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Republic Act 7610 or the "pecial Protection of children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act" will be six years old on July 22, 1997.  This means that six years have passed since the passage of this landmark legislation. Its passage signaled the commitment of the legislature to the improvement in the lives of children in the Philippines. > However, statistics from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) show that in a span of six years there was a250% increase in the number of reported child abuse cases in the Philippines. More specifically, the 1000 cases reported in 1992 ballooned to 3,776 last year. Considering the estimate that reported cases constitute less than 10% of actual abuses commmitted against children, we have reason to be alarmed. rows.author: A027
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE TEACHING OF DISASTER AWARENESS AND DISASTER MITIGATION AS PART OF THE CURRICULUM OF ALL PRIMARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN THE COUNTRY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Philippines is one of the most disaster- prone countries in the world and the need is imminent to promote awarenessd of the hazards concomitant with it.  The Philippine archipelago is particularly prone to earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, typhoons, tsunami, floods and droughtbecause of its geologic and geographical conditions and yet studies done by the NATIONAL CONFERENCE ON NATURAL DISASTER MITIGATION in October 1994 have shown that we, as a people, have been observed to be more reactionary than anticipatory in our disaster-prepar edness and hazard awareness. Planning for a probable disaster is low in the priorities of majority of the population, especially among the low-income bracket whose main preoccupation is daily subbsistence and survivial. Sadly, data from the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center in Thailand shows that in 1994, the world economy lost more money from natural disasters that is spent on development aid.
